```{=html}
  const WALK = [
    /* 0 */ "6142105632464136202012545063215243512043054316434343453143012436124304512652161240513640645601520261412024125101241520530",
    /* 1 */ "614210653246413620201254507b98c9bac897ba7cba8dbabababca8ba7034361243045126521612406136407cbd70620261412024125101241520630",
    /* 2 */ "615210653246414620201254507b98c9bac87053064318cabababca8ba7034361243045126521878a7c8adb7dbcd70620261413024125101241620630",
    /* 3 */ "615230653256414620201264507b98c9bac87053064318cabababca8ba7034361243045129d98d87a7c8adb7dbcd70620298a89215126101251621630",
    /* 4 */ "61523065343ac8ad92101264507b98c9bac87053064329ca9a9baca7ba30353a87ab7ac87dc98d87a36146407cbd70620298a79215126101251621630",
  ];

  const CURVE = [
    /* 0 */ [1000,1000,1000,1000,1000,1000,1000,1000,1000,1000,1000,1000,1000,1000,1000,1000,1000,1000,1000,1000,1000,1000,1000,1000,1000,1000,1000,1000,1000,1000,1000,1000,1000,1000,1000,1000,1000,1000,1000,1000,1000,1000,1000,1000,1000,1000,1000,1000,1000,1000,1000,1000,1000,1000,1000,1000,1000,1000,1000,1000,1000,1000,1000,1000,1000,1000,1000,1000,1000,1000,1000,1000,1000,1000,1000,1000,1000,1000,1000,1000,1000,1000,1000,1000,1000,1000,1000,1000,1000,1000,1000,1000,1000,1000,1000,1000,1000,1000,1000,1000,1000,1000,1000,1000,1000,1000,1000,1000,1000,1000,1000,1000,1000,1000,1000,1000,1000,1000,1000,1000,1000],
    /* 1 */ [1000,1000,976,960,942,926,910,894,880,865,852,839,826,814,802,791,780,769,759,750,740,731,723,714,706,698,691,684,677,670,664,658,652,646,641,636,630,626,621,616,612,608,604,600,596,593,589,586,583,579,576,574,571,568,566,563,561,559,556,554,552,550,548,547,545,543,542,540,538,537,536,534,533,532,531,529,528,527,526,525,524,523,523,522,521,520,519,519,518,517,517,516,515,515,514,514,513,513,512,512,511,511,511,510,510,509,509,509,508,508,508,507,507,507,507,506,506,506,506,505,505],
    /* 2 */ [1000,1000,952,921,888,859,832,807,783,762,742,724,707,691,677,663,651,639,629,619,610,602,594,587,580,574,569,563,559,554,550,546,543,540,537,534,531,529,527,525,523,521,519,518,517,515,514,513,512,511,510,510,509,508,508,507,506,506,506,505,505,504,504,504,503,503,503,503,503,502,502,502,502,502,502,501,501,501,501,501,501,501,501,501,501,501,501,501,501,500,500,500,500,500,500,500,500,500,500,500,500,500,500,500,500,500,500,500,500,500,500,500,500,500,500,500,500,500,500,500,500],
    /* 3 */ [1000,1000,929,883,838,799,765,734,707,683,662,644,627,613,600,588,578,569,561,554,548,542,537,533,529,526,523,520,518,516,514,512,511,510,509,508,507,506,505,505,504,504,503,503,503,502,502,502,502,501,501,501,501,501,501,501,501,501,500,500,500,500,500,500,500,500,500,500,500,500,500,500,500,500,500,500,500,500,500,500,500,500,500,500,500,500,500,500,500,500,500,500,500,500,500,500,500,500,500,500,500,500,500,500,500,500,500,500,500,500,500,500,500,500,500,500,500,500,500,500,500],
    /* 4 */ [1000,1000,905,846,791,746,708,676,648,625,606,589,575,564,554,545,538,532,527,523,520,516,514,512,510,508,507,506,505,504,504,503,503,502,502,502,501,501,501,501,501,501,500,500,500,500,500,500,500,500,500,500,500,500,500,500,500,500,500,500,500,500,500,500,500,500,500,500,500,500,500,500,500,500,500,500,500,500,500,500,500,500,500,500,500,500,500,500,500,500,500,500,500,500,500,500,500,500,500,500,500,500,500,500,500,500,500,500,500,500,500,500,500,500,500,500,500,500,500,500,500],
  ];

  const LAM2 = [1.0000,0.9626,0.9243,0.8850,0.8446];
  const TAU  = [Infinity,26.7,13.2,8.7,6.4];
  const T55  = [-1,62,31,20,15];
  const TWO_M = [84,86,88,90,92];
  const STAY = [Infinity,42.3,21.6,14.5,11.4];
  /* theory 2m/(2 doors) = inf, 43.0, 22.0, 15.0, 11.5 */
  /* b=1 first 120 steps come in blocks of [26, 33, 29, 5, 28] */
  /* step 26: room A 25, room B 1 */
  /* step 40: room A 25, room B 15 */
  /* step 60: room A 27, room B 33 */
  /* step 120: room A 82, room B 38 */

  const DOORS = 4;
  /* Doors 2 and 3 join nodes that do not face each other across the gap, so
     they are bowed clear of both rooms instead of drawn straight through
     them. [from, to, control point or null]. */
  const DOOR = [[0, 7, null], [1, 8, null], [2, 9, [120, 20]], [3, 10, [120, 180]]];
  const TSHOW = 120;             /* steps of WALK on screen */
  const NW = 100;                /* size of the crowd */

  /* ------------------------------------------------------------- geometry --- */
  const PX0 = 34, PX1 = 252, PYT = 18, PYB = 112;
  const PLO = 0.4;                                   /* bottom of the y axis */
  const tx = (t) => PX0 + (t / TSHOW) * (PX1 - PX0);
  const ty = (p) => PYB - ((p - PLO) / (1 - PLO)) * (PYB - PYT);
  const TW = (PX1 - PX0) / TSHOW;                    /* width of one tick */
  const SY = 134, SH = 14;                           /* the strip band */
  const DIG = "0123456789abcd";
  const room = (ch) => (DIG.indexOf(ch) < 7 ? 0 : 1);

  /* --------------------------------------------------------------- scenes --- */
  const scenes = [
    {
      label: "Two rooms, one door",
      note: "Fourteen nodes in two dense rooms, joined by a single edge. Each room holds exactly half the network's edge endpoints, so in the long run the walker has to split its time evenly between them. The whole question is how long the long run is.",
      async run(ctx) {
        ctx.build();
        ctx.setDoors(1);
        const c = ctx.say("the two rooms");
        [["nodes", "7 + 7"], ["edges inside a room", "21 each"],
         ["doors between them", "1"],
         ["each room's share of 2m", "43 of 86"]].forEach((row, i) => {
          const t = ctx.el("div", "anim-tally anim-fade",
            "<span>" + row[0] + "</span><b>" + row[1] + "</b>");
          t.style.animationDelay = ctx.fast() ? "0s" : (0.9 + i * 0.4) + "s";
          c.appendChild(t);
        });
        if (!ctx.fast()) await ctx.sleep(2800);
        c.appendChild(ctx.el("div", "anim-quote anim-fade",
          "equal shares of 2m, so &pi; says the walker spends half its life " +
          "in each room. Nothing in that sentence says when."));
        await ctx.sleep(3200);
      }
    },
    {
      label: "Watch one walker rattle",
      note: "Release the walker in room A and take forty steps one at a time. It stands on the doorway node at steps 5, 17, 19 and 25, turning back inside on the first three; on the fourth it goes through, landing in room B at step 26. Behind it the crowd of a hundred drains out at the same crawl.",
      async run(ctx) {
        const c = ctx.say("one walker, one step at a time");
        const big = ctx.el("div", "anim-big", String(NW));
        c.appendChild(big);
        c.appendChild(ctx.el("div", "anim-caption",
          "of the hundred released with it, still in room A"));
        const verdict = ctx.el("div", "anim-tally anim-fade");
        verdict.style.visibility = "hidden";
        c.appendChild(verdict);

        if (ctx.fast()) {
          ctx.upto(40);
          big.textContent = String(ctx.crowd(40));
          verdict.innerHTML = "<span>first crossing</span><b>step 26</b>";
          verdict.style.visibility = "visible";
          return;
        }

        ctx.upto(0);
        await ctx.sleep(800);
        for (let t = 1; t <= 40; t++) {
          ctx.step(t);
          big.textContent = String(ctx.crowd(t));
          if (t === 26) {
            verdict.innerHTML = "<span>first crossing</span><b>step 26</b>";
            verdict.style.visibility = "visible";
            await ctx.sleep(1500);
          } else {
            await ctx.sleep(t < 8 ? 340 : 165);
          }
        }
        c.appendChild(ctx.el("div", "anim-quote anim-fade",
          "the door was never more than two steps away. But standing in the " +
          "doorway, six of the walker's seven choices lead back inside &mdash; " +
          "which is why a room this size holds it for about forty steps at a " +
          "stretch."));
        await ctx.sleep(3400);
      }
    },
    {
      label: "It moves in blocks",
      note: "Run it out to a hundred and twenty steps. The strip is that one walker's whole history, and it is not a mixture — it is blocks: 26 steps in A, 33 in B, 29 in A, 5, then 28. Averaged over 20,000 steps a block is 42 steps long.",
      async run(ctx) {
        const c = ctx.say("a hundred and twenty steps");
        const big = ctx.el("div", "anim-big", "—");
        c.appendChild(big);
        c.appendChild(ctx.el("div", "anim-caption",
          "of the hundred released with it, still in room A"));

        if (!ctx.fast()) {
          for (let t = 41; t <= TSHOW; t++) {
            ctx.step(t);
            big.textContent = String(ctx.crowd(t));
            await ctx.sleep(38);
          }
        } else {
          ctx.upto(TSHOW);
        }
        big.textContent = String(ctx.crowd(TSHOW));

        [["blocks in those 120 steps", "26, 33, 29, 5, 28"],
         ["average block, over 20,000", "42 steps"],
         ["2m / 2 doors", "86 / 2 = 43"]].forEach((row, i) => {
          const t = ctx.el("div", "anim-tally anim-fade",
            "<span>" + row[0] + "</span><b>" + row[1] + "</b>");
          t.style.animationDelay = ctx.fast() ? "0s" : (i * 0.5) + "s";
          c.appendChild(t);
        });
        if (!ctx.fast()) await ctx.sleep(2400);
        c.appendChild(ctx.el("div", "anim-quote anim-fade",
          "the crowd has evened out; the single walker has not. Its own tally " +
          "over those 120 steps is 82 in room A against 38 in room B, and it " +
          "will stay lopsided for thousands of steps. That is what a community " +
          "<em>is</em>, to a walker."));
        await ctx.sleep(3800);
      }
    },
    {
      label: "Now open more doors",
      note: "Drag the number of doors. With none the walker never leaves and there is no single long-run answer at all. With one it takes 62 steps before the room it started in stops telling you where it is; with four, fifteen. Same fourteen nodes each time.",
      async run(ctx) {
        const c = ctx.say("you set the number of doors");
        ctx.labels("doors", "&lambda;<sub>2</sub>", "&tau;");
        const track = ctx.el("div", "anim-track");
        const knob = ctx.el("div", "anim-knob");
        track.appendChild(knob);
        c.appendChild(track);
        c.appendChild(ctx.el("div", "anim-caption",
          "drag: nought to four doors between the two rooms"));

        const verdict = ctx.el("div", "anim-tally anim-fade");
        verdict.style.visibility = "hidden";
        c.appendChild(verdict);

        const dial = ctx.mountKnob(knob, {
          min: 0, max: DOORS, step: 1, value: 1,
          label: "Doors between the two rooms",
          format: (b) => b + (b === 1 ? " door" : " doors"),
          onGrab: () => ctx.pause(),
          onInput: (b) => {
            ctx.setDoors(b);
            ctx.upto(TSHOW);
            verdict.innerHTML = (b === 0)
              ? "<span>0 doors</span><b>it never leaves</b>"
              : "<span>" + b + (b === 1 ? " door" : " doors") +
                "</span><b>" + T55[b] + " steps to 55%</b>";
            verdict.style.visibility = "visible";
          }
        });

        if (ctx.fast()) { dial.set(DOORS); return; }

        dial.set(1);
        await ctx.sleep(2200);
        dial.set(0);
        await ctx.sleep(2600);
        for (let b = 1; b <= DOORS; b++) { dial.set(b); await ctx.sleep(2000); }
        c.appendChild(ctx.el("div", "anim-quote anim-fade",
          "&tau; falls from 27 steps to 6 as the doors open, and the blocks in " +
          "the strip shorten with it. &ldquo;Slow to mix&rdquo; and &ldquo;has " +
          "communities&rdquo; are not two facts about a network. They are one."));
        await ctx.sleep(4600);
      }
    }
  ];

  mountScenes(document.getElementById("rw-trap"), scenes, {
    stepsLabel: "Trapped-walker steps",

    /* The two things only this animation has: a fourteen-node drawing whose
       doors open and close, and a chart that carries the crowd's curve above
       one walker's timeline. Both are built once, in scene 1, and only
       mutated afterwards — so jumping to a step still lands on a drawing,
       because the kit fast-forwards the earlier scenes first. */
    helpers(ctx) {
      const netBox = ctx.$("[data-rt-net]");
      const plotBox = ctx.$("[data-rt-plot]");
      const side = ctx.$("[data-rt-say]");
      const S = { b: 1, t: 0 };

      const at = (n) => NODE[n][0] + " " + NODE[n][1];

      /* ---------------------------------------------------------- the build */
      function build() {
        S.mode = null;
        S.hot = null;
        netBox.textContent = "";
        plotBox.textContent = "";
        const slow = !ctx.fast();

        /* ---- the two rooms ---- */
        const svg = ctx.svgRoot("0 0 240 200");
        const g = () => svg.appendChild(ctx.svgEl("g"));
        const gShade = g(), gIn = g(), gDoor = g(), gNode = g(), gTok = g(), gName = g();

        gShade.appendChild(ctx.svgEl("circle",
          { cx: 60, cy: 100, r: 54, "class": "rt-room-a" }));
        gShade.appendChild(ctx.svgEl("circle",
          { cx: 180, cy: 100, r: 54, "class": "rt-room-b" }));

        EDGE.forEach((e) => {
          gIn.appendChild(ctx.svgEl("line", {
            x1: NODE[e[0]][0], y1: NODE[e[0]][1],
            x2: NODE[e[1]][0], y2: NODE[e[1]][1], "class": "rt-in"
          }));
        });

        S.door = DOOR.map((d) => {
          const p = ctx.svgEl("path", {
            d: d[2] ? "M " + at(d[0]) + " Q " + d[2][0] + " " + d[2][1] + " " + at(d[1])
                    : "M " + at(d[0]) + " L " + at(d[1]),
            "class": "rt-door"
          });
          p.style.opacity = 0;
          return gDoor.appendChild(p);
        });

        NODE.forEach((q, i) => {
          const n = ctx.svgEl("circle",
            { cx: q[0], cy: q[1], r: 8.5,
              "class": "anim-node" + (i >= 7 ? " rt-node-b" : "") });
          if (slow) {
            n.classList.add("anim-fade");
            n.style.animationDelay = (0.1 + i * 0.05) + "s";
          }
          gNode.appendChild(n);
        });

        const tok = ctx.svgEl("g", { "class": "anim-glide" });
        tok.appendChild(ctx.svgEl("circle", { r: 16, "class": "rt-halo" }));
        tok.appendChild(ctx.svgEl("circle", { r: 10.5, "class": "rt-tok" }));
        tok.style.opacity = 0;
        gTok.appendChild(tok);
        S.tok = tok;

        [[60, "room A", "rt-a"], [180, "room B", "rt-b"]].forEach((r) => {
          const t = ctx.svgEl("text", { x: r[0], y: 192, "class": "rt-name " + r[2] });
          t.textContent = r[1];
          gName.appendChild(t);
        });

        netBox.appendChild(svg);

        S.read = ctx.el("div", "anim-readout anim-readout--tight",
          '<span><i data-la>step</i> <b data-va>0</b></span>' +
          '<span><i data-lb>in A</i> <b data-vb>100</b></span>' +
          '<span><i data-lc>in B</i> <b data-vc>0</b></span>');
        netBox.appendChild(S.read);
        S.la = S.read.querySelector("[data-la]"); S.va = S.read.querySelector("[data-va]");
        S.lb = S.read.querySelector("[data-lb]"); S.vb = S.read.querySelector("[data-vb]");
        S.lc = S.read.querySelector("[data-lc]"); S.vc = S.read.querySelector("[data-vc]");
        [S.la, S.lb, S.lc].forEach((n) => { n.style.fontStyle = "normal"; });

        netBox.appendChild(ctx.el("div", "anim-caption",
          "two 7-cliques and the doors between them &mdash; the two joined " +
          "cliques of the mixing-time section, with two more nodes in each room."));

        /* ---- the crowd's curve, and one walker's timeline under it ---- */
        const psvg = ctx.svgRoot("0 0 260 176");
        const pg = () => psvg.appendChild(ctx.svgEl("g"));
        const gAx = pg(), gCur = pg(), gStrip = pg(), gCursor = pg();

        gAx.appendChild(ctx.svgEl("line",
          { x1: PX0, y1: PYB, x2: PX1, y2: PYB, "class": "anim-axis" }));
        gAx.appendChild(ctx.svgEl("line",
          { x1: PX0, y1: PYT - 4, x2: PX0, y2: PYB, "class": "anim-axis" }));
        gAx.appendChild(ctx.svgEl("line", {
          x1: PX0, y1: ty(0.5), x2: PX1, y2: ty(0.5),
          "class": "anim-marker anim-marker--faint"
        }));
        const lab = (x, y, txt, cls) => {
          const t = ctx.svgEl("text", { x: x, y: y, "class": "rt-num " + (cls || "") });
          t.textContent = txt;
          gAx.appendChild(t);
        };
        lab(PX0 - 5, PYT + 4, "100", "rt-end");
        lab(PX0 - 5, ty(0.5) + 3, "50", "rt-end");
        lab(PX0, PYB + 12, "0");
        lab(tx(60), PYB + 12, "60");
        lab(PX1, PYB + 12, "120 steps", "rt-end");
        lab(PX0 - 5, SY + 10, "walk", "rt-end");

        S.curve = gCur.appendChild(ctx.svgEl("polyline", { points: "", "class": "rt-curve" }));

        S.tick = [];
        for (let i = 1; i <= TSHOW; i++) {
          const r = ctx.svgEl("rect", {
            x: (tx(i - 1) + 0.15).toFixed(2), y: SY,
            width: Math.max(0.9, TW - 0.3).toFixed(2), height: SH
          });
          r.style.opacity = 0;
          S.tick.push(gStrip.appendChild(r));
        }

        S.cursor = gCursor.appendChild(ctx.svgEl("line", {
          x1: PX0, y1: PYT - 6, x2: PX0, y2: SY + SH + 3, "class": "rt-cursor"
        }));
        S.cursor.style.opacity = 0;

        plotBox.appendChild(psvg);
        plotBox.appendChild(ctx.el("div", "anim-caption",
          "line: how many of a hundred walkers released together in room A are " +
          "still there after t steps &mdash; exact, from <b>P</b><sup>t</sup>, " +
          "not a simulation. Band: the one recorded walk on the left, one tick " +
          "per step, coloured by the room it is in."));

        setDoors(1);
        upto(0);
      }

      /* How many doors are open. Everything downstream — the drawing, the
         curve, the strip — is a lookup on b. */
      function setDoors(b) {
        S.b = b;
        S.door.forEach((p, i) => { p.style.opacity = i < b ? 1 : 0; });
        if (S.mode === "doors") {
          S.va.textContent = String(b);
          S.vb.textContent = b === 0 ? "1.000" : LAM2[b].toFixed(3);
          S.vc.textContent = b === 0 ? "∞" : TAU[b].toFixed(1);
        }
      }

      function crowd(t) { return Math.round(CURVE[S.b][t] / 10); }

      function place(n, glide) {
        S.tok.style.opacity = 1;
        if (!glide) S.tok.classList.remove("anim-glide");
        S.tok.style.transform = "translate(" + NODE[n][0] + "px," + NODE[n][1] + "px)";
        if (!glide) {
          S.tok.getBoundingClientRect();          /* commit before re-arming */
          S.tok.classList.add("anim-glide");
        }
      }

      /* The curve drawn as far as step t, and the readouts that go with it. */
      function paint(t) {
        S.t = t;
        const pts = [];
        for (let i = 0; i <= t; i++) pts.push(tx(i).toFixed(1) + "," + ty(CURVE[S.b][i] / 1000).toFixed(1));
        S.curve.setAttribute("points", pts.join(" "));
        S.cursor.style.opacity = t > 0 ? 1 : 0;
        S.cursor.setAttribute("x1", tx(t));
        S.cursor.setAttribute("x2", tx(t));
        if (S.mode !== "doors") {
          S.va.textContent = String(t);
          S.vb.textContent = String(crowd(t));
          S.vc.textContent = String(NW - crowd(t));
        }
      }

      /* One step of the recorded walk: the token moves, its tick is inked, and
         the door it used flashes if it changed rooms. */
      function step(t) {
        const w = WALK[S.b];
        const now = w[t], was = t > 0 ? w[t - 1] : null;
        place(DIG.indexOf(now), t > 0 && t < 8);
        if (t > 0) {
          const q = S.tick[t - 1];
          q.style.opacity = 1;
          q.setAttribute("class", room(now) === 0 ? "rt-tick-a" : "rt-tick-b");
          if (was !== null && room(now) !== room(was)) flash(DIG.indexOf(was), DIG.indexOf(now));
          else cool();
        }
        paint(t);
      }

      /* Lay the walk down to step t with no animation — the fast-forward path,
         and the way the knob scene repaints a whole strip at once. */
      function upto(t) {
        const w = WALK[S.b];
        cool();
        for (let i = 0; i < TSHOW; i++) {
          const q = S.tick[i];
          if (i < t) {
            q.style.opacity = 1;
            q.setAttribute("class", room(w[i + 1]) === 0 ? "rt-tick-a" : "rt-tick-b");
          } else {
            q.style.opacity = 0;
          }
        }
        if (t > 0) place(DIG.indexOf(w[t]), false); else S.tok.style.opacity = 0;
        paint(t);
      }

      function flash(from, to) {
        cool();
        const i = DOOR.findIndex((d) =>
          (d[0] === from && d[1] === to) || (d[1] === from && d[0] === to));
        if (i >= 0) {
          S.hot = i;
          S.door[i].setAttribute("class", "rt-door rt-door-hot");
        }
      }
      function cool() {
        if (S.hot != null) S.door[S.hot].setAttribute("class", "rt-door");
        S.hot = null;
      }

      function say(title) {
        side.textContent = "";
        const c = ctx.el("div", "anim-panel anim-pop");
        if (title) c.appendChild(ctx.el("div", "anim-caption", title));
        side.appendChild(c);
        return c;
      }

      /* S is filled by build(), i.e. after helpers() has already run, so
         everything reaching into it has to be a function — the kit copies
         these onto ctx by value at mount time. */
      return {
        build: build, say: say, setDoors: setDoors, step: step, upto: upto,
        crowd: crowd,
        /* The third scene hands the readout row over to the knob, so the row
           can carry doors / lambda2 / tau instead of steps and counts. */
        labels: function (a, b, c) {
          S.mode = "doors";
          S.la.innerHTML = a; S.lb.innerHTML = b; S.lc.innerHTML = c;
          setDoors(S.b);
        }
      };
    }
  });
});
</script>
```

Every method in this section is a different way of charging for that delay.

### Modularity Is a Short Walk Minus a Long One

Modularity can be interpreted through random walks [@delvenne2010stability]:

$$
Q = \sum_{ij} \left(\pi_i P_{ij} - \pi_i \pi_j \right) \delta(c_i, c_j)
$$

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Where this comes from — three lines of algebra"}
Modularity as it is defined in Module 5 makes no mention of walks at all:

$$
Q = \frac{1}{2m} \sum_{ij} \left( A_{ij} - \frac{d_i d_j}{2m} \right) \delta(c_i, c_j)
$$

Push the constant $1/2m$ inside the bracket, then split each term so that a factor of $d_i/2m$ appears in front:

$$
\frac{A_{ij}}{2m} = \underbrace{\frac{d_i}{2m}}_{\pi_i} \cdot \underbrace{\frac{A_{ij}}{d_i}}_{P_{ij}} = \pi_i P_{ij},
\qquad
\frac{d_i d_j}{(2m)^2} = \underbrace{\frac{d_i}{2m}}_{\pi_i} \cdot \underbrace{\frac{d_j}{2m}}_{\pi_j} = \pi_i \pi_j .
$$

Substituting both gives the random-walk form. Nothing was assumed — modularity was a statement about random walks all along; we simply had not yet met $\pi_i = d_i/2m$ and $P_{ij} = A_{ij}/d_i$ to recognise it.
:::

where:

- $\pi_i = \frac{d_i}{2m}$ is the stationary distribution of the random walk
- $P_{ij}$ is the transition probability between nodes $i$ and $j$
- $\delta(c_i, c_j)$ is 1 if nodes $i$ and $j$ are in the same community, 0 otherwise

Read the two terms as two clocks on the same pair of nodes:

1. $\pi_i P_{ij}$ is the probability that a walker in the stationary state is at $i$ and is at $j$ **one step later**.
2. $\pi_i \pi_j$ is the probability that it is at $i$ now and at $j$ **after so many steps that it has forgotten $i$** — equivalently, the chance of finding two independent long-run walkers at $i$ and at $j$.

The $\delta(c_i, c_j)$ keeps only pairs inside the same community. So modularity is: how much more often a short walk stays inside a community than a long walk would by chance. High modularity means walkers linger.

::: {.column-margin}
@delvenne2010stability extends modularity to multi-step random walks, replacing "one step later" with "$t$ steps later", which identifies communities at different resolution scales.
:::

### Infomap Compresses the Trajectory

While modularity provides one approach to community detection through random walks, **Infomap** offers an information-theoretic perspective [@rosvall2008maps; @rosvall2009map].

Infomap asks: *how can we most efficiently describe the path of a random walker through a network?* The key insight is that if a network has strong community structure, a walker spends most of its time within communities and makes only occasional jumps between them. Such a trajectory can be *compressed* using a two-level code:

1. **Module code**: a unique identifier for each community
2. **Exit code**: a special symbol indicating that the walker leaves a community
3. **Node code**: identifiers for nodes within each community

Node names can then be reused across communities — like street names that repeat in different cities — so the description gets shorter exactly when walks stay put. Infomap searches for the partition that minimizes the average number of bits needed to describe the walk.

### Walktrap Turns the Trap Into a Distance

Infomap compresses a trajectory. **Walktrap** [@pons2005computing] uses the same trapping intuition more directly, as a similarity measure.

The idea: run short random walks of a fixed length $t$ from every node. If two nodes are in the same community, a walker starting at either one ends up in roughly the same places, so their $t$-step distributions look alike. Define the distance between nodes $i$ and $j$ as the difference between their $t$-step distributions (scaled by degree), then agglomerate nodes bottom-up, always merging the pair that increases this distance least.

The choice of $t$ matters, and it sets the scale. Small $t$ sees only local structure; large $t$ washes everything out toward the stationary distribution, which knows nothing about communities. Somewhere in between the walk is long enough to explore a community but too short to escape it — and that is where communities become visible.

## Structure Shapes How a Walk Behaves

Everything above depends on the network the walker is placed on. Four cases are worth having in mind:

- **Regular networks** (a lattice, a ring): the stationary distribution is uniform, since all degrees are equal. Mixing is slow, because the walker can only diffuse outward one step at a time — it takes on the order of $N^2$ steps to cross a ring of $N$ nodes.
- **Small-world networks**: the shortcuts from Module 2 dramatically speed up mixing. A few long-range edges let the walker jump across the network instead of crawling around it, which is the dynamical counterpart of the short path lengths we measured there.
- **Scale-free networks**: hubs dominate the stationary distribution, since $\pi_i \propto k_i$. Mixing is fast — almost every walk passes through a hub within a couple of steps, and from a hub anywhere is reachable. Hitting times are strongly asymmetric, as discussed above.
- **Networks with community structure**: mixing is slow, and slow for an informative reason. The walker is trapped inside its community for a long time before escaping, which shows up as a small spectral gap — the $0.073$ we computed for the two joined cliques. This is the property Infomap and Walktrap exploit; the "defect" *is* the signal.

## What You Can Now Do

You started with a drunkard who understood nothing about the city. You can now say precisely what the drunkard measures:

- Write down the transition matrix $\mathbf{P} = \mathbf{D}^{-1}\mathbf{A}$ of any network and say what one step, two steps and $t$ steps mean.
- State and check the stationary distribution $\pi_i = k_i/2m$, and say when it fails to exist.
- Read a spectral gap as a mixing time, and a small gap as a bottleneck.
- Compute return times from $\pi$, and explain why hitting time is asymmetric while commute time is not.
- Explain, in one sentence each, how PageRank, modularity, Infomap, Walktrap and node2vec are all the same walk with different rules.
